newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem says to issue bond for Argentine pensioners.
newsitem.headline: Menem says to issue bond for Argentine pensioners.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said Thursday the government will ask the country's private pension funds to buy bonds to be issued to cover backdated pension payments.

"I have arranged to invite the pension funds to buy a new bond that will offer some (basis) points more than the average earned by the funds to reward their savers," Menem wrote in an article published in daily La Nacion.
"At the same time, this placement which will start by paying off 20 percent of the payments owed this year and will cancel out the debt completely during my mandate.
"This will make it possible to pay our pensioners in cash," Menem said.

The decision to issue bonds comes after Argentina's Supreme Court ruled in December to reestablish the mobility of pensions in line with increases in the cost of living. The ruling in the case by 70,000 pensioners decided that state pensions from 1991 to 1994 will be adjusted upwards by 13.8 percent.
The government has given no estimate on how much will have to be paid to the pensioners but private economists think the figure could be several billion pesos.
Since this debt issue had already been planned it will not affect Argentina's fiscal targets agreed with the International Monetary Fund, Menem said.
